News.title: Terrifying moment massive billboard collapses crushing woman to death inside car as pedestrians sprint to safety
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a massive billboard suddenly collapses and crushes a woman to death inside a car as people in its path run for their lives.

Footage shows the huge sign tipping forward after it became unattached, before slamming to the ground on a busy road.



Pedestrians standing where the billboard was due to crash down can be seen ducking and diving to get out of the way of the falling object.

In the sickening moment of impact, the billboard bounces as it hits the car allowing pedestrians extra seconds to escape.



The driver of the car, María del Carmen Piña Arce, was killed when the billboard crushed her vehicle.

The CCTV footage shows a cement mixer truck manoeuvring beside the billboard seconds before the sign came crashing down.



In the aftermath of the tragedy, the heavily dented white car can be seen poking out from under the collapsed sign.

Emergency crews and ambulances can be seen gathering around the site of the horrific collapse that took place in Mexico City on Friday.



The 53-year-old victim was a teacher and therapist who specialised in addiction recovery, TMZ reported.

The driver of the cement truck, identified in Mexican media as Carlos N, was arrested and charged with manslaughter and property damage.

The man’s bail was reportedly set at 250,000 pesos and he was released until trial.

An investigation to determine how events unfolded and the driver’s responsibility reportedly remain ongoing.

The construction company operating at the site has not assumed civil responsibility for the tragic accident, local outlet Enfoque reports.



The tragedy unfolded on the outskirts of Mexico City, near the Plaza Interlomas shopping centre, according to local media.

A red car travelling ahead of the victim’s white vehicle escaped being crushed by just seconds.

News.title: Will Russia attack Britain? Sabotage, assassinations & spies…How Putin could unleash hell over Brit-made drone strikes
News.content:
RUSSIA has ramped up its thinly veiled threats towards Britain with experts revealing how Vladimir Putin’s latest warnings could spiral into a terrifying new conflict.

The Kremlin’s volatile war of words has drastically escalated this week as Russia said the UK faces “consequences” for supplying drones used by Ukraine for devastating attacks.



Putin’s Foreign Minister, Sergei Lavrov, lashed out at Andy Burnham after the PM made it clear the UK is 100 per cent behind Ukraine against Putin’s “illegal war”.

Lavrov later warned that UK interests “in any part of the oceans” would now be seen as under threat due to the UK’s supporting Kyiv.



He said in a chilling threat on Russian TV: “I feel sorry for Britain if it stays with Ukraine to the bitter end… this only means one thing.”

It came just a day after Russia’s embassy in London warned the UK would face “consequences” for sending their allies long- range Nyan jet drones.



Analysts believe the latest threat points toward potential strikes on British shipping to avenge June’s seizure of the sanctioned Russian “shadow fleet tanker” Smyrtos in Dorset.

The Kremlin has already accused Britain of “acting as an accomplice and co-perpetrator” of “bloody crimes committed by Ukrainian neo-Nazis”.



Simon Diggins, a retired colonel in the British Army turned security, defence and military analyst, says the Kremlin’s colourful language is cause for concern.

He told The Sun: “Britain tends to get this kind of really hyperbolic, aggressive and violent language threatening consequences.

“At every stage when we provided the Ukrainians with major weapon systems, they’ve threatened dire consequences.

“In the past they’ve talked about firing a missile which they call Satan, to drop nuclear weapons into the into the Irish Sea, creating tidal waves that would sweep across across Britain.

“This is normal from them and I don’t think that’s necessarily to be taken seriously directly, however, I think it does indicate how angry they are.”



Simon believes there is a real chance Russia will begin to ramp up aggressive tactics against the UK in the coming months.

Earlier this week, Russia was revealed to have deployed a warship armed with cruise and hypersonic missiles in the Baltic Sea.

The vessel is sat within striking distance of both the UK and its Nato allies.



The Admiral Kasatonov, a frigate with nuclear-capable Zircon hypersonic missiles, was seen last week off the coast of Fehmarn following Kremlin threats to attack British and EU vessels.

Robert Tollast, an expert on land warfare from RUSI, warned Russia could attack the UK by launching drone swarms from ghost ships off Britain’s coast.

He explained: “A lot of large energy and industrial infrastructure is located by the sea.

“So it’s not out of this world to imagine drones being launched by ship at these targets, perhaps hidden in shipping containers.”

Undersea cables providing vital communication links to the UK could also be at risk of Russian attack.



Simon continued: “We could expect a direct reaction, for example, an uptick in the use of their spy trawlers over our submarine cables

“Aggressive cyber operations being employed against us, information operations, subversion, and anything up to sabotage.

“We’ve also had assassinations on our soil and that is to be expected when you’re dealing with Russia because that’s part of their language, how they operate.”

Russia provoking Britain is just ‘tip of the iceberg’ By Jerome Starkey RUSSIA provokes Britain every single day, warns Defence Secretary Wes Streeting. But the goading goes mostly unseen by the public. Hinting at the secret briefings he receives in his new job, Streeting said what is in the public domain is “only the tip of the iceberg”. Speaking to The Sun on a visit to Ukraine, Streeting said: “Incidents like buzzingairspacee or the shooting in the Channel are performative, irresponsible and designed to provoke. “It does at least provide the ­British with a visible manifestation of the day-to-day provocations that we see from Russia every day.” Streeting insisted the only response was to stand up to Russian aggression. Reflecting on Ukraine’s experience, he said: “With tyrants like Putin — if you compromise, they come back for more.” Read more here.

Political analyst Vlad Vexler told The Sun: “Putin thinks of his war with Ukraine as a proxy war in which he’s essentially facing all of the West.



“And the UK is a bee in the bonnet for the regime.

“What they think is wrong with the West is maximally exemplified by the UK in the view of the Kremlin regime.”

Western governments have reportedly pledged over £280billion in military, financial, and humanitarian aid to Ukraine since Russia‘s invasion in 2022.

The US remains Kyiv’s most crucial ally but European nations such as Germany, France and Poland have also played a major role.

Britain prides itself as one of the leading donors to Ukraine as well – much to the Kremlin’s fury.



Just last month, Burnham announced a new £3billion military package to Kyiv which comes alongside dozens of new lethal and non-lethal weaponry and equipment.

Tanks, air defence systems, artillery, and long-range precision strike missiles are all allowed to be used by Ukraine in their fight against Russia.

The UK has also committed to training up Ukrainian fast jet pilots “for as long as it takes”, Burnham pledged.



This sustained support has only dragged Russian-UK relations lower and lower as they war continues to rage on with daily bombardments.

Vexler said this has created a “mythical ideological picture” about the evil West which has been exemplified by the UK due to its involvement.

Vexler, who was born in the Soviet Union before moving to the UK, was quick to add that the threats of a genuine major attack on the UK are “extraordinarily low probability events”.

Simon has also warned that Putin may not even be the biggest worry for the UK within the Kremlin.

He said: “I think what’s even more concerning is whether or not the kind of aggressive violent language is misinterpreted by one of Putin’s subordinates.



“The Kremlin’s general intent is pushed out by Putin but then he leaves subordinates to get on with it from there.

“That has a danger that they may do something which they think is fulfilling what Putin wants them to do.”

Vexler added: “Putin has some very special views, and some of the people around him have some very special views about the UK.”

Russia’s new threats came as its forces launched a missile strike on Pechenihy in the Kharkiv region which killed 10 and injured eight.

The attack on the civilian area blasted 10 private homes, a café, a post office, a store and at least seven cars.

Russia’s latest strikes have further highlighted concerns that the UK has no effective ground-based shield against a Russian ballistic missile or drone swarm attack.

Defence analysts have repeatedly warned that major cities could be left largely unprotected against ballistic strikes as the Labour government struggles to revamp the nation’s defence.

News.title: Young girl got ‘tangled in fishing net’ in sea at Shoreham when ‘family jumped in to try & save her’ before 3 drowned
News.content:
A GIRL got tangled in a fishing net before her desperate family jumped in after her – causing three of them to drown in the choppy sea.

Eyewitnesses described the “mayhem” at Shoreham harbour as a teen girl and her two parents tragically perished on the West Sussex coast.



The family of four were swept out to sea during the frantic bid to save the younger daughter, who is currently fighting for her life in hospital.

Witnesses told how local fishermen alerted police to Britain’s latest water tragedy after spotting the girl in trouble at around 3pm yesterday.



Joe Chrisp, 24, said: “One of the local fishermen said it was two adults, two kids. One of the kids apparently got caught in a fishing net.”

Within minutes, emergency crews including eight ambulances, lifeboats and two helicopters had descended on the shingle beach.

Speaking yesterday, Chief Supt James Collis said all relatives entered the water together for a swim before getting into difficulty.

Officers have not yet named the victims but said their next of kin had been informed and were being supported by specialist officers.



Police are not searching for anyone else, but an investigation has been launched to understand the full circumstances of the tragedy.

One resident claimed that the family had been camping near the harbour in recent weeks.

They told The Telegraph: “I heard from friends in the coastguard that it was a family who had been living in tents by the harbour front.



“They were camping just between the harbour arm and the fort. They have been there for a couple weeks, I’ve walked my dog past them.

“People don’t usually camp there.”

Horrified beachgoers watched as crews battled in vain and carried out CPR after the victims were dragged back to shore.

Anna Peacock, 81, who lives near Kingston Beach across the water from Shoreham, said emergency services were on the scene very quickly.

She said: “It was terribly sad to know that just across the road people have lost their lives.



“People come down to swim, particularly in the summertime and I don’t think they realise there’s a riptide along here.

“It’s very inviting to come to the sea, but the tide could carry you out in seconds, and I don’t think people have realised that.”

Victoria Flint, of nearby Horsham, was there with husband Gary and their children.

She said: “We arrived at about three and soon after we heard the siren for the lifeboat.

“We watched it launch and then, about 20 minutes later, it came back. Ambulances started arriving.



“More and more of them. Then the air ambulances started.”

Locals also described the weather as very windy, and said that the sea appeared to be choppy during the horror.

Joss Loader, who represents Shoreham Beach Residents’ Association on Adur District Council, said there is a “strong sense of shock” in the area.

She said: “Obviously people are really concerned for the young girl.

“A small tightly knight community with a very deep sense of shock and that sense of disbelief you get after a tragedy…



“It has come out of nowhere.”

The RNLI confirmed it had launched rescue boats from Shoreham Harbour at 2.51pm.

Two more followed from the nearby Brighton station shortly after 3pm.

A coastguard helicopter joined the search at 2.45pm, along with three more rescue teams.

Aerial images showed the lifeboat returning as two air ambulances and scores of paramedics waited at the station.



East Worthing and Shoreham MP Tom Rutland said the community “will be hoping and praying for the recovery of the young girl”.

He wrote: “I am deeply saddened by the tragic news that three people have died following an incident in the water near Shoreham Fort this afternoon.

“My thoughts are with the family and friends of those who have lost their lives.”

Figures from the Department of Work and Pensions show approximately 20,000 more migrants were claiming Universal Credit in May 2026 than last year.



The record high follows Reform UK’s vow to stop foreigners claiming benefits if the party came to power.

News.title: Police reveal cause of death of girl, 17, found stuffed in suitcase after being ‘murdered by loner tourist’ in Thailand
News.content:
COPS have revealed the cause of death for a teenage girl whose body was found inside a suitcase in Thailand.

The naked body of Tunchanok Donhomla, 17, was found dumped near railway tracks in Pattaya on June 27.



Australian expat Simon Peter Carman, 45, has been charged with the murder of the teenager.

Thai cops have now revealed that autopsy results found that the teen suffered a brain injury and died of suffocation, 7News report.



Superintendent Colonel Anek Srathongyoo said: “The autopsy report said that [Tunchanok] had a brain injury and she suffocated.

“She had no other injuries.”

Carman allegedly met Tunchanok, known locally as “Cake”, near Pattaya beach after drinking at a red light district bar until about 2am on June 25.

Police allege they got into an argument about money and claim Carman previously said he “may have strangled her, causing her to lose consciousness and eventually die”.



CCTV footage shows Carman and Tunchanok entering his apartment at 03:34 am and later that evening he can be seen walking alone carrying a large suitcase.

Cops said they had collected Carman’s DNA and matched it to DNA found on Tunchanok’s body.

Anek added that the DNA match “likely came from when he put her body in the suitcase”.

Police are hopeful that the investigation will conclude by August 21, as they must indict Carman by September 18 .

Carman has been charged with murder, which in Thailand, is punishable by death or life in prison.



He also faces three other charges; concealing or moving a body, kidnapping a child over 15 but under 18, and taking away a child over 15 but under 18 for an indecent act.

Following his arrest, Carman denied the charges against him, claiming he had “acted in self defence”.

In a video recorded in custody, Carmen apologised to Tunchanok’s family saying he felt bad and that it was “out of [his] control.”

He added: “I know you’ll be very sad, upset… same [as] me.

“Please tell other girls… just to be careful.”



Thai police are also investigating possible links between three previous bodies found in suitcases.

They emphasised that there is no evidence linking Carman to the deaths, but detectives are investigating the similarities.

One victim was found in September 2025, stuffed inside a suitcase with gym weights attached at the Khlong Bang Phai Reservoir, Chonburi.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In February 2025, a fisherman in Rayong discovered a floating suitcase containing a naked dead woman body, believed to be in her 30s, and heavy weights to weigh down the bag.

A red suitcase was also found in January 2025 near Highway No. 331 in Chonburi, with dumbbells and the remains of a woman, also believed to be in her 30s.

News.title: Bride-to-be, 29, mauled to death by bear after being dragged out of tent in middle of night while camping with fiance
News.content:
SAVAGED BY BEAST Bride-to-be, 29, mauled to death by bear after being dragged out of tent in middle of night while camping with fiance

A BRIDE-TO-BE has been savaged by a bear after she was dragged from her tent in the dead of night – just one day after getting engaged.

Snezhana Korolyova, 29, was mauled to death during a romantic camping trip in the Altai Mountains of Russia in southern Siberia.



Her fiance – who has not been named – had only proposed the day before she was tragically killed.

The couple were awoken to the beast tearing apart their tent around 1am before it “hauled the screaming woman away”.



It savagely killed the newly engaged woman before carrying her body across the Biya River to bury her, according to reports.

Gamekeepers and Russian cops shot in the air but did not aim at the beast despite “having the opportunity to kill it” due to shooting restrictions in the area.

read more world news GRIZZLY HORROR Zookeeper famous for kissing bears has arm ripped off by beast in attack

A witness named Alina said: “It wouldn’t give her up and… dragged her across the river.”

“It’s horrific. Her boyfriend is in shock — he had only just proposed to her.”



Snezhana’s remains were reportedly found at the site where the animal had buried her with officials only able to access it once the beast was frightened away.

From the Novosibirsk region, the savaged woman was an employee of Russia’s Emergencies Ministry and had been staying with her fiance at the Istok holiday campsite in Artybash village.

Locals said around 20 bears routinely roam around the village.



Alina continued: “What infuriated people most was that, despite having the opportunity to kill a man-eating bear, the uniformed officers fired into the air, citing a ban on shooting at a target within a populated area.

“How does that make sense?”

Another camper said her sister narrowly escaped the same bear that night.

She said: “We came face to face with it. My sister fell over and crawled into a hut while lying on the ground.

“A man who happened to be driving past saved her. What a hero!



“He shone his headlights at the bear and it ran across the road. He even dented his car’s wing hitting it.”

The bear remains at large, according to local reports.

A ten-day “state of alert” was issued for the village following the horror attack.

A representative of the Mayminsky District Society of Hunters and Fishermen said the slashing of hunting days for wild animals led to an increase in bear attacks.

He said: “The hunting season was shortened to 30 days. Because of this, the bear population has begun to increase.



“There’s little hunting, the bears are reproducing, and the food supply is scarce — nuts are scarce — so they simply come out to hunt people when they’re hungry.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Altai Republic prosecutor’s office has opened an inquiry into the woman’s death.

It comes as a brother and sister were mauled to death in India after a bear attacked them in a field.

News.title: Six in 10 are desperate to try new hobbies but lack confidence, time & cash, poll finds
News.content:
HOBBY HURDLES Six in 10 are desperate to try new hobbies but lack confidence, time & cash, poll finds

SIX in 10 Brits have hobbies they’re desperate to try – but they’re held back by lack of money, time, confidence and not knowing where to start.

A poll of 2,000 adults found learning a language, playing a musical instrument and writing – whether that’s a book or a blog – are the top things they hope to do one day.



Painting or drawing, photography and pottery are also aspirations, as are padel, line dancing and foraging, while slightly more left-field goals include ghost hunting, axe throwing and circus skills.

But along with limited finances (33 per cent), time (28 per cent) and self-belief (24 per cent) – and getting started (24 per cent), 10 per cent are hindered by fears they’ll be judged by others.



The research was commissioned to celebrate the partnership between Davina McCall’s podcast, Begin Again and Monzo, which has launched its new ‘Get busy living’ platform.

They’re hosting free events this September and October including rave Pilates in Manchester, a wellness event in Cardiff, line dancing in London and public speaking workshops in Edinburgh.

Speaking about the findings, Davina said: “So many people have things they’ve always wanted to try, but the hardest part is taking that first step – whether that’s finding the time, the confidence, or just knowing where to start.

“It’s even harder when you feel like you’re doing it alone.



“That’s exactly why we’ve built ‘Get busy living’ with Monzo – to help Brits make time for the things they love, and to create spaces where people can connect with like-minded communities and stop putting their passions on hold.”

It also emerged 17 per cent don’t have anyone to do their would-be hobby with or aren’t comfortable doing it alone and 16 per cent worry they’re too old to pursue their goals.

On average those polled have five experiences, challenges, hobbies or skills they’ve always wanted to do or try but haven’t yet.

With those polled owning three pieces of equipment or kit for hobbies they’ve never or rarely used.

Among those yet to embark on particular goals, the study found not doing so has resulted in feelings of regret (32 per cent), frustration (24 per cent) and fears they’ve missed out (24 per cent).



Although the research carried out through OnePoll found 71 per cent are open to change – having reinvented themselves in some way twice on average to date.

And 33 per cent have a desire to reinvent themselves, with 46 per cent simply ready for a change and 36 per cent keen to make up for lost time.

Other reasons for wanting to ‘relaunch’ themselves include retirement, children growing up, and moving home.

With changing career (seven per cent) and the end of a long-term relationship (six per cent) also motivations.

But any desire to change among those polled might be countered by a lack of confidence, with self-belief dropping steadily with age.



Around six in 10 Gen Zs (59 per cent) feel more self-assured now than they did 10 years ago, but this falls to 46 per cent among Millennials, 26 per cent among Gen X and 13 per cent among Boomers.

When it comes to regional differences, more than anywhere else those living in London have hobbies they want to try but haven’t started (82 per cent).

This is followed by the West Midlands (64 per cent), Scotland and the North West (both 61 per cent).

With the lowest number living in Northern Ireland (56 per cent) – but this could be because more of those living there have fulfilled such ambitions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Monzo’s AJ Coyne said: “Whether it’s the nerves before going to your first class alone, finding time for a new hobby, or working out how to budget for the things you love, there are plenty of reasons people put their passions on hold.



“Get busy living is about making sure money isn’t one of them. We want everyone to have the confidence and freedom to do more of what they love, without financial admin getting in the way.”

News.title: Moment horrified passengers watch on helplessly as their train passes just yards from huge fire at London waste facility
News.content:
THIS is the moment horrified passengers helplessly watch on as their train passes just yards from a huge fire at a London waste facility.

Fifteen fire engines and around 100 firefighters descended on the raging inferno in Deptford on Tuesday night.



Shocking footage captured by terrified passengers showed their carriage edging past the plant, which was completely engulfed in flames on Landman Way.

One clip shows a huge orange fireball and towering plumes of black smoke billowing into the sky which could be seen from miles around.





The passengers watched on in awe with the flames remarkably close to their train.

Fire crews scrambled to the scene shortly before 8pm and brought the fire under control in the early hours of this morning.



Speaking from the scene on Wednesday morning, Station Commander Duncan Rees said: “Crews worked hard in difficult conditions to bring the fire under control.

“One of the Brigade’s 32m ladders and a 64m ladder were used as a water towers to tackle the flames from above.

“Whilst the fire is under control, crews will remain on scene into the morning and afternoon as they work to extinguish the remaining pockets of fire.”



The cause of the fire is not yet known.

London Fire Brigade said that around 50 tonnes of household waste were involved in the blaze and that the building’s structure had been “severely damaged”.

Dramatic images captured the chaotic aftermath of the fire with the building reduced to a burnt-out shell.

Mountains of debris can be see piled up as firefighters worked to battle back the remaining flames in the early hours of this morning.

Local residents were urged to keep the doors and windows closed on Wednesday night.



The fire also sparked travel chaos with lines travelling between London Bridge, Canada Water, New Cross and New Cross Gate affected.

Almost all trains in and out of London Bridge station were either delayed or cancelled.

Hoards of passengers could be seen waiting for buses, desperately trying to find alternative routes.



Other footage showed shocked witnesses filming the flames as they tore through the building.

A massive orange fireball could be seen raging at the plant, illuminating the London skyline.

A London Fire Brigade spokesperson said: “Fifteen fire engines and around 100 firefighters responded to a fire on Landman Way, Deptford.

“The fire involved around 50 tonnes of household waste stored at a waste facility. The structure of the facility has been severely damaged by the fire.”

They added: “The Brigade took the first of over 160 calls reporting the incident at 1959, and crews from East Greenwich, Old Kent Road, Deptford and surrounding fire stations were sent to the scene.

“Firefighters had the fire under control by 0216 (August 19), and are now working to extinguish the remaining pockets of fire, and dampen down the scene.

“The cause of the fire is not yet known.”

News.title: Travel expert Simon Calder issues crucial advice to one group heading abroad
News.content:
Travel expert Simon Calder issues crucial advice to one group heading abroad

Travel expert Simon Calder has advice for those heading abroad

View 3 Images Travel expert Simon Calder has issued advice to young people (Image: BBC)

Students celebrating their A-level results are being urged to think carefully about safety before setting off on gap years and adventures abroad.

‌



Travel expert Simon Calder has issued a stark warning to young people preparing to head overseas – telling them that risk management should be at the heart of their plans. Calder, speaking on The Travel Expert podcast with Telegraph journalist Greg Dickinson, said he wanted students to return home “in one piece with nothing but happy memories”.

‌



His advice comes as thousands of young people consider gap years, holidays or trips abroad before starting university. Calder, who took a gap year himself, said there was plenty to gain from seeing the world – but warned that students and their parents should not overlook the potential dangers.

‌



View 3 Images Calder's first warning was about alcohol and recreational drugs (Image: South_agency via Getty Images)

His top three concerns are: drugs and drink, accidents in water and road safety. Calder said: “If you are going to go on a gap year, the main thing to do is risk management.”

He added: “I am absolutely concerned to try to make sure that everybody comes back in one piece with nothing but happy memories.”

‌



Drugs, drink and the risk of spiking

Calder's first warning was about alcohol and recreational drugs. He acknowledged that many people drink and some take recreational drugs, but urged travellers to understand the risks – including the possibility of their drink being spiked.

He also specifically warned students about methanol poisoning, which has tragically killed travellers overseas. His message was not simply to avoid excessive drinking or drugs, but to understand the potentially serious consequences of what can happen abroad.

And students should never allow alcohol or drugs to lead them into taking unnecessary risks. Calder warned against doing things such as hiring a scooter or going for a midnight swim after consuming drink or drugs.

‌



Take care around water

Calder's second major warning was about accidents in water. Young travellers heading to beaches, islands and other holiday destinations are urged to understand the dangers posed by strong currents.

One particular hazard is a rip current – a powerful current of water moving away from the shore which can quickly carry swimmers out to sea. Calder said travellers should “make absolutely sure that you know how to identify a rip tide” and understand what to do if caught in one.

The important message is not to panic or try to fight directly against the current.

‌



View 3 Images Calder's second major warning was about accidents in water (Image: South_agency via Getty Images)

Road safety

Calder stressed there was one danger that sat “absolutely top of my risk list” , which is road safety. He warned that road risks can increase sharply once travellers leave Britain.

“As soon as you leave the UK, risks start to multiply on the roads,” he said. His advice was to consider how you are going to travel around a country before setting off.

‌



He suggested that, where appropriate, using trains or flying in countries with high road accident rates could reduce the risks faced by young travellers. Calder's warning is particularly relevant to gap-year students who may be tempted to hire scooters or motorcycles as a cheap and convenient way of getting around.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Thailand warning

The discussion also turned to Thailand, a hugely popular destination for young British travellers. Dickinson warned that students should not assume the country is a place where drug use is tolerated simply because of its reputation for parties and nightlife.

Article continues below

He specifically highlighted the famous Full Moon parties – but stressed that Thailand has strict drug laws. Travellers can face serious consequences for possessing or taking illegal drugs. Dickinson said: “They're extremely strict on drugs, so you basically need to not get involved with that whatsoever.”

News.title: Brits warned as popular Greek holiday photo spot leaves two tourists injured
News.content:
Brits warned as popular Greek holiday photo spot leaves two tourists injured

Holidaymakers warned viral airport photo trend can turn dangerous in seconds

View 5 Images The short and narrow runway attracts holidaymakers (stock image) (Image: Getty)

British holidaymakers are being warned against copying viral plane-spotting videos at a popular Greek island airport. It comes after two tourists were seriously injured by jet blast within days of each other.

‌



Skiathos International Airport, officially called Alexandros Papadiamantis Airport, has become one of Europe’s most famous plane-spotting locations because its runway sits extremely close to the coastline and surrounding public areas. Aircraft pass remarkably low over spectators as they approach, attracting holidaymakers who gather nearby to photograph and film arrivals and departures. It features a short, narrow runway measuring 5,341 feet.

‌



But two recent incidents have highlighted the risk when aircraft are taking off. On August 10, a 52-year-old Italian tourist suffered serious head injuries after the force from a departing aircraft reportedly knocked her to the ground.

‌



She was initially treated at the Skiathos Emergency Clinic before being airlifted to Volos General Hospital. Just three days later, another Italian woman in her early 50s reportedly suffered a severe arm fracture after being knocked over by the jet blast from another departing aircraft.

Local authorities and the airport have consistently placed large warning signs around the perimeter fence to emphasise the serious risks of being near departing aircraft. The prominent signs displayed around Skiathos International Airport, Alexandros Papadiamantis, alert onlookers that the force of engine thrust can push people and objects away. Police and city officials keep reminding visitors to avoid congregating directly behind the runway.

View 5 Images One woman was airlifted to Volos General Hospital for further medical treatment (stock image)

‌



Emily Matthews, travel advisor at Private Portugal Tours, says tourists should understand that standing near a runway to watch a plane land and positioning themselves directly behind an aircraft preparing to depart can expose them to very different risks. "The videos that make Skiathos famous can make the whole experience look like an unusual holiday attraction, but tourists need to pay attention to exactly where they are standing and what the aircraft is doing," Emily said.

"Standing directly behind a departing aircraft to get a dramatic video is something holidaymakers should avoid. If there are warning signs telling you about jet blast, take them literally and move away."

Take off is where tourists need to be particularly careful

Skiathos has sometimes been described as Europe’s answer to St Maarten, where aircraft famously pass low over a beach before reaching the runway. That close approach is what many tourists travel to photograph.

‌



However, watching aircraft take off can be more hazardous for spectators too close to the runway perimeter, as large aircraft generate substantial thrust as they depart. Warning signs at Skiathos specifically alert visitors to the danger of jet blast.

"People may arrive because they have watched a video of an aircraft flying low overhead, then assume that anywhere around the runway is part of the same experience," Emily said. "The important distinction is what happens when a plane turns around and prepares to take off. If you are positioned behind it, you can suddenly be in the path of extremely powerful airflow.

"Do not choose your position because a video looked impressive from there. Look at the warning signs around you and keep well away from areas where spectators are being warned about jet blast."

‌



View 5 Images Warning signs cautioning pedestrians about dangerous jet blast from departing aircraft are seen at the end of the runway near Skiathos International Airport

Do not assume the crowd means the spot is safe

Plane spotting at Skiathos is well established, and large numbers of spectators can gather close to the airport. Emily says that creates another risk for tourists: assuming that a location must be safe because dozens of other people are already standing there.

"A crowd is not a safety assessment," she said. "It is very easy on holiday to think, 'Everyone else is doing it, so this must be where you are supposed to stand.'

‌



"That logic can be especially persuasive when people have their phones out and appear to be waiting for exactly the same photograph. But warning signs do not stop applying because a crowd has formed beside them."

The August 10 incident is currently being investigated by local authorities, according to reports. The tourist was believed to have been standing at a plane-spotting area close to the airport when she was knocked down. Skiathos has also seen jet-blast injuries in previous years, reinforcing that the hazard is not theoretical.

View 5 Images The location is known for low-flying aircraft and attracts aviation enthusiasts and tourists.

‌



The 'perfect' video is not worth standing behind a departing aircraft

Emily also warns tourists against trying to recreate footage they have seen online frame-for-frame. Viral travel videos often show only the few dramatic seconds when an aircraft passes or begins its take-off roll. They do not necessarily show the warnings around the location, how far the person filming is from the aircraft or what happened immediately afterwards.

"Social media can flatten the difference between watching something and participating in the risk," Emily said. "You might see people’s clothes and hair being blown around and think that is part of the fun. Once enough videos like that circulate, being hit by the blast can almost become part of the attraction.

"Two serious injuries within days should be enough to remind people that being knocked off your feet is not a harmless holiday experience." She advises tourists who want to watch aircraft to choose a position away from the direct line behind departing planes, respect barriers and signs, and move if local staff or authorities instruct spectators to do so.

‌



View 5 Images Jet engines create super fast streams of air. These blasts are incredibly powerful (stock image)

Keep children away from the jet-blast area

Families should be particularly cautious about bringing young children into crowded plane-spotting locations where departing aircraft are nearby. "Children are naturally going to be excited when a huge aircraft passes close overhead, but this is one place where parents should decide where the family stands rather than simply following the crowd.

"If you cannot clearly understand the warnings or you are unsure whether your position is exposed to departing aircraft, move farther away. You can still enjoy watching the planes without trying to stand in the most dramatic possible spot.

Article continues below

"Skiathos is famous for an extraordinary view that aviation enthusiasts cannot experience at many other European destinations. That does not make every position around the runway equally safe. The simplest rule is to remember the difference between the spectacular low approach people travel to see and putting yourself behind an aircraft as it powers up to leave. A holiday video is never worth ignoring a warning sign for."

News.title: Premium dog food brand issues recall after pets develop ‘extremely painful’ condition
News.content:
Premium dog food brand issues recall after pets develop ‘extremely painful’ condition

The company has urged dog owners to stop feeding the food to their pets immediately following reports of suspected eye conditions

View 2 Images Premium dog food brand issues recall after pets develop ‘extremely painful’ condition (Image: Su Arslanoglu via Getty Images)

A premium pet food brand has issued a voluntary recall of its dog food after receiving numerous reports of suspected eye problems in dogs. Years, a subscription service providing fresh dog food tailored to individual pets' needs, contacted customers via email to reveal it had identified a "potential" link between its buckwheat ingredient and a dry eye condition.

‌



The company, which claims its fresh meals are prepared by chefs, urged owners to immediately stop feeding Years products to their pets, following reports of suspected dry eye cases.

‌



The company said on its website: "As a precaution, we're issuing a voluntary recall of all Years Fresh Meals (excluding Chef's Collection).

‌



"This follows a small number of reports of dogs having a potential adverse eye reaction to buckwheat, a common and approved ingredient, which we include in our meals. As of August 16, this has affected 0.1% of our customers.

"We know for some, this will strike as overly cautious, but at Years, we will always put every dog's health and wellbeing first."

"Your subscription is paused for six weeks, and we will be reformulating our recipes without buckwheat."

‌



In place of buckwheat, the brand will switch to quinoa, with subscribers set to receive a thank-you gift with their next delivery.

Dog owners were strongly advised to stop feeding Years fresh meals "immediately", regardless of whether their pet is showing symptoms. The company also warned British customers against feeding the meals to other animals, or donating and selling them.

View 2 Images Dog owners are urged to keep an eye out for symptoms (Image: Getty)

‌



The company confirmed it will arrange a free collection of any unused meals and issue a full credit to the pet owners' accounts for the order.

Symptoms to watch out for include excessive blinking or squinting, thick discharge, and persistent pawing at the eyes.

Dogs may also display signs of general discomfort around the eyes. Should any of these symptoms appear, contact your vet and mention this recall.

‌



The PDSA (People’s Dispensary for Sick Animals) states that dry eye is a lack of tear production.

Their website states: “It’s an extremely painful condition that, left untreated, can lead to conjunctivitis, eye ulcers and in severe cases, permanent scarring, or even loss of an eye. In most cases, dry eye in dogs is immune-mediated, meaning that the body accidentally destroys its own tear glands.

“The damage tends to be gradual over a period of months to years, so if the condition is diagnosed and treated early enough, it can usually be well-controlled with medication.”

‌



Anyone with queries can reach Yours via their website , email, WhatsApp, or SMS.

Dog owners flocked to social media to voice their concerns, with one person writing on TikTok : "My cockapoo has been on Years since January. She was diagnosed with dry eye in May. I feel so guilty."

Another said: "I'm appalled that they are only offering credit. I don't want my dog to eat this food anymore."

Article continues below

A third commented: "I'm so upset for all the owners and dogs who have been affected. It's breaking my heart reading the Facebook comments."

News.title: Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as controversial star issues grovelling apology
News.content:
Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as controversial star issues grovelling apology

Nick Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in Mallorca June, with the Australian now admitting that he made a 'huge mistake' and pledging to 'come back better'

View 2 Images Nick Kyrgios has apologised following his provisional ban (Image: TPN/Getty Images)

Tennis star Nick Kyrgios has issued a grovelling apology after testing positive for cocaine. Kyrgios, 31, has been provisionally suspended following the test which took place at the ATP 250 tournament in Mallorca in June.

‌



His International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) provisional suspension has been in place since August 4, with cocaine being banned in competition under anti-doping rules. Kyrgios has the right to appeal the ban but has not done so at the time of writing, and he's taken 'full responsibility' for the 'huge mistake', pledging to 'come back better'.

‌



The Australian wrote on his Instagram story: "I wanted you to hear this from me first. I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine. I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

‌



"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Emma Raducanu could QUIT tennis over injury hell, claims BBC icon READ MORE :

Carlos Alcaraz issued US Open warning as injury comeback plans in balance READ MORE :

"I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

‌



"I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did.

"However, the good news is that this has given me a wake up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

View 2 Images Nick Kyrgios last played at Wimbledon in July (Image: Matthias Hangst/Getty Images)

‌



"I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family. I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick."

Under the terms of his suspension, Kyrgios cannot play, coach at or even attend Grand Slams or events which are sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours. The 31-year-old has been restricted to just four singles matches this season, with knee and wrist injuries hampering his career in recent years.

Kyrgios, who reached a career-high rank of 13, last played at Wimbledon in the men's doubles. He partnered Kazakhstan's Alexander Bublik but they were knocked out in the first round, losing to Mate Pavic and Marcelo Arevalo.

News.title: Dr Amir Khan issues warning to anyone wearing a fitness watch at night
News.content:
Dr Amir Khan issues warning to anyone wearing a fitness watch at night

The health expert addressed concerns about fitness watches showing 'low levels' at night

View 2 Images The NHS GP says your watch could be picking up on an important health issue (Image: No Appointment Necessary/YouTube)

Dr Amir Khan has issued a warning to anyone who uses a fitness watch, especially at night, explaining how it may pick up on something that definitely warrants booking a doctor's appointment. The advice was shared in the latest episode of his No Appointment Necessary podcast, which he hosts alongside presenter Cherry Healey.

‌



During the episode, the NHS GP and resident ITV doctor discussed what to do if a fitness watch detects oxygen levels (SPO2) dropping below 90% during the night. He warns that this may indicate sleep apnoea.

‌



The medical condition causes a temporary obstruction of the airway, leading to poor sleep quality. He says that while the accuracy of individual watches may vary, such readings should be taken as a serious potential sign of health issues that can strain the heart and lungs - potentially causing other issues, like high blood pressure. He recommends undergoing a professional sleep study for a definitive diagnosis.

‌



Many of today's fitness watches and smartwatches can measure blood oxygen levels, commonly known as SpO2 or Pulse Ox. They work by using light sensors located on the back of the watch that emit red and green light into your skin, then measure how much light bounces back from your blood.

These gadgets are designed to track overall fitness and wellness. They aren't medical devices, so they shouldn't be relied upon to diagnose health issues. Factors like movement, cold skin, tattoos, or a loose fit can also lead to inaccurate readings.

‌



Reading out a question from a viewer, Cherry asked Dr Amir Khan: "How serious should we take the night measurements of our fitness watches?" The doctor replied: "I can't speak to how accurate your individual watches are, but they're probably a good enough indication. They might not be 100% accurate, but they're probably picking up something that's dropping."

He warned: "If your oxygen levels are dropping through the night, it usually means you've got something called sleep apnoea. You stop breathing altogether for a very short period of time and then you wake up."

Dr Amir Khan continues: "With sleep apnoea, you get complete obstruction of your upper airway briefly, and then you wake up a little bit enough to open up your airway again. And so in that moment, your oxygen levels will drop. It's that which is the issue, and that is why you wake up not feeling refreshed.

‌



"But also that chronic dropping of oxygen through the night can lead to increased pressure on your heart. It can lead to high blood pressure and long-term issues as well. So if you are getting those readings on your watch, I would first of all ask your partner, 'Am I making this noise?' But if it's not the case, your doctor can refer you for something called sleep studies, where they will monitor your oxygen while you sleep, and they'll give you a definitive answer."

View 2 Images Sleep apnoea could cause other health problems, like high blood pressure, a higher chance of having a stroke and type 2 diabetes (stock image) (Image: Getty)

The NHS says: "Sleep apnoea is when your breathing stops and starts while you sleep. The most common type is called obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). Sleep apnoea needs to be treated because it can lead to more serious problems."

‌



What problems can sleep apnoea cause?

Sleep apnoea can also be difficult for your partner and put a strain on your relationship with them. Without treatment, sleep apnoea can lead to other problems, including:

high blood pressure

a higher chance of having a stroke

type 2 diabetes

heart disease

depression or mood changes

a higher chance of having a serious accident caused by tiredness, such as a car accident

difficulty concentrating at work or school

You may need to tell the DVLA about your sleep apnoea. If sleep apnoea with excessive sleepiness has been confirmed, you must not drive until symptoms like feeling very tired are under control. Check the rules for driving if you have sleep apnoea on GOV.UK.

‌



What are the main symptoms of sleep apnoea?

Symptoms of sleep apnoea mainly occur during sleep. They include:

your breathing stopping and starting

making gasping, snorting or choking noises

waking up a lot

loud snoring

During the day, you may also:

‌



feel very tired

find it hard to concentrate

have mood swings

have a headache when you wake up

How is sleep apnoea treated?

The NHS says: "Sleep apnoea can sometimes be treated by making lifestyle changes like losing weight, giving up smoking and reducing how much alcohol you drink. But many people need to use a device called a CPAP machine. You'll be given this for free on the NHS if you need it." Other treatments sometimes used for sleep apnoea include:

News.title: Popular sun cream declared 'high risk' now 'banned from sale' in UK
News.content:
Popular sun cream declared 'high risk' now 'banned from sale' in UK

The products have been rejected at the UK border

View 2 Images A popular brand of sun cream has been rejected at the UK border (Image: Carlos Barquero/Getty)

A popular brand of sun cream has been branded "high risk". The Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) has issued a notice for the product, stating it was rejected at the UK border.

‌



Bubble Cosmetics Sunscreen Pack has been given a "high risk" rating by the OPSS. It said: "The product presents a risk due to inadequate labelling and traceability information.

‌



"Multiple mandatory cosmetic labelling requirements have not been met, including omissions relating to sunscreen use instructions and product traceability. As a result, consumers may not have sufficient information to use the product appropriately, and effective regulatory traceability is impaired."

‌



It added: "The product does not meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 (‘the Cosmetics Regulation’)." As a result, the products have been rejected for entry into the UK and therefore cannot be sold to customers.

View 2 Images Bubble Cosmetics Sunscreen Pack has been recalled (Image: OPSS)

The sun cream came from the United States. Bubble is sold in a range of UK retailers, including Boots and Asos. The affected items are a range of Bubble sun cream products packaged in yellow cardboard boxes.

‌



The Mirror has contacted Bubble for comment.

Earlier this month, a brand of wet wipes was urgently recalled due to contamination risks. The OPSS explained that the wipes may be microbiologically contaminated, meaning they could cause adverse skin reactions.

FreshWipes Intimate Unscented Wipes were sold on the FreshWipes website, Amazon UK, TG Jones (formerly WH Smith), TikTok Shop and QVC. It is described as a 10-pack of moist wipes, which are also sold in multipacks and in self-care bundles.

‌



The OPSS said: "It has been identified that affected batches may be microbiologically contaminated, with the preservative system not performing as required.

"This could result in users experiencing adverse skin reactions. The affected batches do not meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 (the ‘Cosmetics Regulation’).

"The product has been recalled from end users by FreshWipes. Consumers who have an affected batch should stop using the product immediately. Contact your place of purchase for instructions on return or disposal of product and refund/redress."

Article continues below

FreshWipes said: "Check the batch number printed on the back of the pack. If it reads LOT 0926 or LOT 0515, the product is part of this recall.

"What to do: Please stop using the affected product immediately. If you have purchased Freshwipes Intimate Wipes from Batch LOT 0926 or LOT 0515, please contact our customer support team at Sales@freshwipes.co.uk with a photo of your remaining packs clearly showing the LOT number.

"We apologise for any inconvenience caused and remain committed to the safety and quality of our products."

News.title: UK heatwave prompts unusual discovery as woman finds bat floating in her TOILET
News.content:
UK heatwave prompts unusual discovery as woman finds bat floating in her TOILET

The bat, later nicknamed Louis, is believed to have flown in through an open window as it searched for water during the UK heatwave - volunteers later took the animal in and nursed it back to health

View 3 Images The bat was found inside a toilet (Image: Sussex Bat Group / SWNS)

As Britain sweltered in another heatwave one woman made an unusual discovery when she found a bat floating in her toilet.

‌



The animal, which was later nicknamed Louis, was discovered floating in the loo having flown in through an open window. According to experts, it had likely been searching for water during the heatwave.

‌



Dehydrated and left in a weakened state after his ordeal, the bat was carefully rescued from the bathroom in Sussex using a garden trowel before being dried off. Sussex Wildlife Trust's Bluesky channel pointed the finder towards expert advice and she called Sussex Bat Group volunteers.

‌



View 3 Images The bat was left in a weakened state (Image: Amanda Millar / Sussex Bat Hospi / SWNS)

BBC viewers hooked on new series perfect for David Attenborough fans READ MORE :

RSPCA says 1 type of food will attract foxes to your garden in August READ MORE :

The woman, who didn't wish to be named, said: "I’ve learnt so much about bats from this wonderful and unsought encounter with a beautiful wild creature, including that so many are dehydrated and that the biggest single cause of injury is cats, who lurk outside their roosting places. And that they can find refuge in the tiniest gaps under hung tiles and in other nooks and crannies on older buildings."

Little Louis was later taken into the care of Sussex Bat Hospital's Amanda Millar, who confirmed he was a serotine - one of the UK's largest bat species. While thin and exhausted on arrival, a week of rest and steady diet of mealworms restored him to full health and ready for a test flight, proving he was fit enough to return home.

‌



View 3 Images The bat made a full recovery (Image: Amanda Millar / Sussex Bat Hospi / SWNS)

At dusk, Louis was driven back to the garden where he was found and released. He flew off over the honeysuckle and into the night, with a bat later spotted flitting across the darkening sky, possibly Louis finding his way home. Sussex Wildlife Trust is reminding residents that summer heatwaves can leave bats dehydrated and searching for water in unexpected places.

Article continues below

Anyone who finds a bat in distress is encouraged to contact their local Bat Group for advice. According to the UK Bat Conservation Trust, the serotine is one of the first to appear in the evening, often when it is still somewhat light outside.

It has a wingspan of 32cm to 38cm and they usually hunt within 2km of where they roost - but may forage up to 6km further afield. After catching something like a large beetle, the serotine will slowly fly around, chewing on its prey and dropping the wing cases and legs. It tends to fly at around tree-top height, 10m or so, often close to vegetation.

Sometimes the bats will 'flop' with their wings outstretched onto foliage in order to catch large insects and will feed around street lamps - they have even been known to catch prey from the ground. They mainly roost in buildings, and are hardly ever found roosting in trees.

News.title: Major UK motorway speed camera glitch 36k fines cancelled - full list
News.content:
Major UK motorway speed camera glitch 36k fines cancelled - full list

Speed cameras on major UK motorways are still flashing drivers — but police are dropping all the fines

View Image Smart motorway cameras in the UK have a glitch, meaning speeding fines are not being issued (Image: Getty)

More than 36,000 speeding fines have been cancelled - because of a fault with 154 speed cameras. The problem, which impacts 12 motorways in the UK, was discovered last October - and led to thousands of fines being cancelled.

‌



Now police have refused to push through more than 36,000 speeding tickets - and cancelled the fines, The Times reported. The problem impacts all Smart Motorways in the UK including the M1, M6, M5 M25 and M42.

‌



Last year, a “technical anomaly” was identified with 154 speed cameras used on all smart motorways - meaning that there was a delay between the cameras and the speed limits being changed. This saw drivers being sent speeding fines after the limit had changed - meaning they were not breaking the law.

‌



Officials confirmed the cameras are still flashing on the motorways - but police have lost confidence and are not enforcing the fines. National Highways, the government body in charge of England’s major roads, said that it had identified 2,650 instances of “erroneous camera activations” since 2021 but police forces across the country were so concerned that they cancelled more than 36,000 ongoing and historic speeding cases related to the cameras.

The Times reported that more than ten months after the national issue was identified, the malfunctioning cameras are still being put through testing by the Home Office and have not yet been approved for use.

While they wait for approval, police forces are not issuing any enforcement notices for speeding motorists caught by the faulty cameras. In January, shortly after the camera flaws were exposed, Nick Harris resigned as chief executive of National Highways after five years in charge with sources stating that he had lost the board’s confidence.

‌



Major Motorways with Smart Sections

M1: Multiple upgraded stretches between Junction 6A and Junction 42 (including J prejudicial areas like J10-13, J16-19, and J28-31).

M3: Junction 2 to Junction 4A (Surrey and Hampshire).

M4: Junction 3 (Hayes) to Junction 12 (Theale) [0.10].

M5: Sections around Junction 4A to 6 and Junction 15 to 17 (Bristol region).

M6: Extensive segments running from Junction 2 up to Junction 19 (including the heavily monitored West Midlands and M6 J10A-13 corridor).

M20: Controlled and dynamic sections between Junction 3 and Junction 7.

M23: Junction 8 to Junction 10 (south of London toward Gatwick).

M25: Large continuous and controlled segments spanning from Junction 2 round to Junction 30 (notably J5-7 and J23-27).

M27: Junction 4 to Junction 11 (Hampshire).

M42: Junction 3A to Junction 9 (the original pilot region around the West Midlands).

M60: Junction 8 to Junction 18 (Greater Manchester ring road).

M62: Sections covering Junction 10 to Junction 12 and Junction 18 through to Junction 30 (Manchester to Leeds)

The independent review ordered by Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, into the agency’s handling of the issue is due this summer but is yet to be published. Simon Williams, from the RAC, said: “It’s very concerning that this has not been fixed and that so many speeding drivers are not facing the consequences. We urge the government to address this as a matter of priority.”

A National Highways spokesperson said: “Speeding offences continue to be detected and prosecuted. A range of enforcement measures are in place to help keep road users safe. A fix for the impacted cameras is going through rigorous testing.”

‌



In a statement at the time the Goverment said: “National Highways has confirmed an anomaly has been identified in the way some variable speed cameras interact with signs on some A roads and motorways.

“This has resulted in a very small number of people incorrectly facing enforcement action for speeding. The anomaly has meant there was at times a slight delay between cameras and variable speed signs, leading to some drivers being incorrectly detected as speeding after the limit had changed.

“As a result, National Highways have identified approximately 2,650 total erroneous camera activations on impacted roads since 2021, which is the equivalent of fewer than 2 a day. Anybody affected will be contacted directly by the relevant police force. They will be reimbursed and have points removed from their licence where relevant.“

‌



What are smart motorways?

Smart motorways are motorways which use technology to manage traffic flow.

In addition to informing drivers of speed limits - which are regulated using speed cameras - the overhead signs can also alert people to accidents or other hazards ahead.

There are three main types:

News.title: Jump in energy bills drives UK inflation to highest rate for four months
News.content:
Higher energy bills drove UK inflation up to 2.9% in the year to July, the highest level in four months, according to new figures.

Gas prices soared at the sharpest pace in almost four years, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, leading to an increase in the cap on household energy bills in July. Energy costs surged after US-Israel war with Iran began, which has restricted global oil supplies.

July's reading is the highest since March but some price growth slowed. Food inflation, at 1.3%, is at its lowest rate for close to five years.

Experts said the inflation figure is unlikely to influence the Bank of England to change its key interest rate at its next meeting in September.

Energy costs for households rose on 1 July after Ofgem, the energy regulator, increased the price cap on gas and electricity costs by 13%, which added Â£221 a year to the typical bill.

Homes are forecast to see a 4% rise in energy bills from October, according to Cornwall Insight, which would take them to the highest level since July 2023.

Therre is ongoing uncertainty over the US-Iran conflict, which has seen effective closures of the Strait of Hormuz, a key trading passage for ships carrying oil, liquefied natural gas and other commodities.

Cornwall Insight, an independent energy consultancy, added that energy price pressures were being compounded by the ongoing heatwave across Europe "increasing gas demand for power generation to meeting air conditioning and cooling demand".

News.title: Burnham unveils plan to get rough sleepers off streets for Christmas
News.content:
Every rough sleeper in England will be offered accommodation this winter, the prime minister has said.

Andy Burnham made ending rough sleeping his first pledge when entering Downing Street in July and now says he wants "to get everyone in for Christmas".

Emergency accommodation will be provided to end the need for rough sleeping alongside practical support for any health needs, as part of a Â£442m package.

Conservative shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said Burnham promised to end rough sleeping in Greater Manchester when mayor of the area but "failed because he didn't do the hard work necessary".

Burnham's pledge seeks to build on the success of Everyone In, a Covid pandemic-era scheme that saw thousands of rough sleepers housed in hotels and temporary accommodation.

About 37,000 people were helped by that scheme, following its launch in March 2020. The charity Shelter found that about a quarter of them had found settled accommodation, in the form of housing lasting at least six months., external

The PM's announcement comes with an additional Â£102m in new funding, taking Burnham's total commitment to tackling rough sleeping to Â£442m since becoming prime minister.

The money is said to be "fully funded" within the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

As well as providing immediate support to get people off the streets, the funding is also designed to deliver more than 1,000 homes over the next three years to provide rough sleepers with permanent accommodation.

The funding will also provide "intensive wraparound support", typically psychiatric and drug and alcohol services to help people rebuild their lives.

Burnham said: "We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again. But it needs all of us.

"Government will put the money in. But I'm asking leaders in communities and sectors across society to play their part locally too."

The government said areas facing the greatest pressures will get the largest share of support.

It added guidance will make clear the need to ensure "adequate and accessible provision" for female rough sleepers, who it says are often underrepresented in official statistics and can be at greater risk of violence, abuse and exploitation.

News.title: Tennis player Nick Kyrgios suspended after testing positive for cocaine
News.content:
In a lengthy statement on Instagram, Kyrgios said the last few years of injuries had taken "a huge toll on me, both mentally and physically".

"My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do," he wrote.

"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

"None of that excuses what I did."

Kyrgios said he would be stepping away from social media and public life for the next 28 days to "focus on getting myself right".

Cocaine is classified as a stimulant and substance of abuse on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list.

Reduced sanctions apply for athletes who test positive for the substance out of competition.

However, Kyrgios' sample was submitted during a tournament in which he played singles, ultimately losing in the first round to Adam Walton.

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me," Kyrgios added.

"Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

Kyrgios has long been a controversial figure in tennis.

His behaviour on court has been widely criticised and he has been given numerous large fines for smashing racquets, making audible obscenities and arguing with the umpire.

In 2023, he admitted assaulting an ex-girlfriend two years earlier. He avoided a criminal conviction.

He was criticised further for making a series of comments which have been considered misogynistic.

In 2024 he shared a post from controversial influencer Andrew Tate. He later said he had gone "to all lengths" to distance himself from the self-proclaimed misogynist.

Kyrgios was also critical of the handling of two high-profile anti-doping cases involving top players Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek, calling them "disgusting" for tennis.

Kyrgios has won seven ATP Tour singles titles and reached the Wimbledon final in 2022, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.

He and compatriot Thanasi Kokkinakis won the Australian Open men's doubles title together in 2022.

Kyrgios has also spoken about his struggles with mental health, saying he "genuinely contemplated" suicide and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London after losing at Wimbledon in 2019.

News.title: Thunderstorm warnings issued for parts of UK with flash flooding expected
News.content:
Yellow thunderstorm warnings have been issued across the UK, with heavy showers expected to lead to flash flooding and travel disruption.

The Met Office warnings will come into force across northern England, Northern Ireland and eastern Scotland later in the day on Wednesday. The warning for northern England will remain in place until Thursday morning.

The downpours follow almost two months of dry weather, with parts of the country experiencing their first rain in weeks on Tuesday.

People in areas impacted by thunderstorms have been told by the Met Office to expect that businesses and homes could flood, transport services could be delayed and power cuts are likely.

The yellow weather warnings are in place for:

Northern Ireland from 12:00 until 23:59 BST on Wednesday

Parts of North East Scotland, including Aberdeen, from 14:00 until 21:00 on Wednesday

Parts of the North of England, including Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, from 19:00 until 10:00 on Thursday
