World.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El Gobierno trabaja en el traslado urgente de 500 niñas migrantes de Ceuta a la Península
World.content:
El PP pide la reprobación de cinco ministros por la gestión de la crisis migratoria en Ceuta

Alicia García, portavoz del PP en el Senado, ha anunciado que su partido presentará una moción de reprobación a cinco ministros: Fernando Grande-Marlaska (Interior), José Manuel Albares (Exteriores), Margarita Robles (Defensa), Mónica García (Sanidad) y Ana Redondo (Igualdad) por la gestión de la crisis migratoria en Ceuta. “Lo que ocurrió allí no fue un incidente más, fue una ocupación premeditada y sin precedentes en el territorio español. Y lo que es más grave es que el Gobierno lo sabía y no hizo nada”, ha atacado este miércoles en una rueda de prensa desde la Cámara alta.

La portavoz popular ha detallado los motivos de la moción de reprobación para cada ministro: a Marlaska por “sostener que la normalidad había llegado en 24 horas, cuando 20 días después siguen sin estar en esa normalidad” en la ciudad autónoma; a Albares, porque se desconocen los pormenores de la negociación con Marruecos; a Robles por no comparecer finalmente en el Senado; a Mónica García por “el colapso sanitario” en la ciudad autónoma; y a Ana Redondo, porque “no ha pisado Ceuta ni un solo día, y eso que las agresiones sexuales se han multiplicado por ocho”.

“Las sillas vacías en el Senado no pueden quedar impunes”, ha dicho García sobre la incomparecencia en la Cámara alta de Albares, Marlaska y Robles, que decidieron no acudir a dar explicaciones sobre la crisis ceutí tras la citación del PP. “Pedro Sánchez querría un Senado amordazado, vaciado y paralizado”, ha criticado la portavoz popular para después afirmar que “gracias a la mayoría del PP hemos reprobado a ocho ministros; hoy vamos a por más, por el enésimo desplante de Sánchez a los españoles”.

World.title: Portugal se adelanta a España y abre una consulta pública para regular el coste del ‘escudo antiapagón’
World.content:
La Entidad Reguladora de los Servicios Energéticos (ERSE) de Portugal puso en marcha el mes pasado un proceso de consulta pública con el objetivo de “contener la volatilidad de costes” de la llamada operación reforzada del sistema eléctrico que se aplica tras el apagón del año pasado, “mejorar su previsibilidad y garantizar la sostenibilidad económica del sistema eléctrico”. La audiencia pública de ERSE, homóloga portuguesa de la Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC) española, se inició el pasado 10 de julio y permanecerá abierta hasta el 10 de septiembre y en ella puede participar cualquier persona o entidad interesadas.

Según fuentes del sector eléctrico, la iniciativa sitúa a Portugal por delante de España en el debate regulatorio sobre unos costes que han ganado protagonismo tras el apagón que afectó a la Península Ibérica el 28 de abril de 2025 y los efectos de la tormenta Kristin en enero de 2026. Ambos acontecimientos obligaron a reforzar los criterios de seguridad y operación de la red, incrementando notablemente los llamados servicios de ajuste del sistema para garantizar el equilibrio instantáneo entre generación y consumo, subraya ERSE en su propuesta. La operación reforzada consiste en la programación masiva de energía síncrona (ciclos combinados de gas, principalmente), que resulta más cara y controla de forma dinámica la tensión de las redes, algo que no hacen por el momento las renovables.

En su iniciativa, el regulador energético portugués considera que la actual evolución de estos costes “exige una respuesta estructural” y propone un paquete de medidas destinadas a reducir la incertidumbre para las empresas y familias. La principal novedad que plantea es la modificación de la forma en que se financian estos costes. Así, ERSE considera que una parte relevante de los importes asociados se debe incorporar progresivamente a los peajes regulados de acceso a las redes (parte fija de la factura de la luz con que se financian las líneas de distribución y transporte) y sacarlos del término de la energía. El objetivo del regulador portugués es integrar hasta el 40% de estos costes en la parte regulada de la factura, comenzando ya en el último trimestre de 2026 con una aplicación gradual.

Junto a esta medida, el regulador luso también plantea actuaciones para reducir la volatilidad de los costes de operación. Entre ellas destaca “la creación de reservas de energía contratadas con las centrales los ciclos combinado de gas” y “la creación de herramientas de cobertura financiera, permitiendo a los agentes cubrirse frente a futuros incrementos de los costes derivados de la operación del sistema”. El sobrecoste de los servicios de ajuste tras el apagón afecta a las comercializadoras eléctricas que al firmar contratos fijos, generalmente por un año, deben trasladar dichos costes a sus clientes pero desconocen su evolución a futuro. Ello les obliga a contratar coberturas que encarecen aún más la factura de sus clientes.

Fuentes empresariales consideran que la iniciativa sitúa a la industria consumidora portuguesa por delante de la española. Y aseguran que el debate “también ha ido ganando intensidad en España, donde empresas, consumidores e industria vienen reclamando soluciones regulatorias que permitan contener unos sobrecostes que ya representan una parte creciente de la factura eléctrica”.

De hecho, el Observatorio del Coste de los Servicios de Operación, del que forman parte la asociación de las grandes eléctricas, Aelec, de comercializadoras independientes, grandes consumidores y las patronales CEOE y Cepyme, entre otros, viene alertando de los costes adicionales que soportan los consumidores y reclama que se implante, al igual que plantea Portugal, mecanismos regulatorios de financiación que estabilicen y minimicen estos importes a hogares e industria. Según el último informe de este observatorio correspondiente a la primera quincena de agosto, los servicios de operación de REE suman ya 3.360 millones en lo que va de este año, un 36% más respecto al mismo periodo del año pasado.

En el sector consideran que la consulta pública portuguesa supone un precedente regulatorio que podría convertirse en referencia para España, donde empresas, consumidores e industria reclaman desde el año pasado medidas que permitan compatibilizar la seguridad del sistema con una factura eléctrica más estable, predecible y competitiva, tal y como se hace en la mayoría de los países europeos. Los costes asociados a la operación del sistema eléctrico son uno de los componentes de la factura eléctrica que más se ha encarecido en los últimos meses. Estos incluyen los de la operación reforzada de REE, pero que esta compañía no desglosa.

Las comercializadoras españolas también habían solicitado a la CNMC y el Ministerio de Transición Ecológica un cambio para que los costes adicionales del sistema tras el apagón se incluyan en algún concepto regulado (además de los peajes de acceso a las redes existen los cargos, que determina en este caso el ministerio). O, cuando menos, que se fije dicho coste para un periodo determinado y se ajuste posteriormente, con el objeto de saber cuánto deben cobrar a sus clientes y cubrirse financieramente. El regulador se opuso en su día a los cambios que reclamaban las compañías y tampoco el ministerio que dirige Sara Aagesen ha dado ningún paso en este sentido.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Por Mónaco sin datos en el móvil ni wifi, la mejor manera de recorrer el Principado
World.content:
Del Casino de Montecarlo a la catedral, pasando por Le Rocher y el Palacio Principesco, esta pequeña ciudad-estado hay que pasearla sin distracciones

En mis artículos para El Viajero no suelo usar la primera persona. Sin embargo, en esta ocasión procede hacerlo, no tanto como aviso para navegantes, sino para que se entienda mejor lo narrado.

A lo largo de los últimos años he visitado en más de una ocasión el Principado de Mónaco, al que es muy fácil llegar con el tren que bordea la Costa Azul, hallándose, por ejemplo, a menos de media hora de Niza. Mi primera vez en la patria de Raniero y Grace Kelly vino precedida de un vendaval de optimismo. Recordaba consejos de profesores del pasado, bien felices de narrar al alumnado cómo esta ciudad-estado consta de unos dos kilómetros cuadrados de superficie total, lo que hace suponer un fácil dominio de ese espacio, poblado por poco más de 38.000 habitantes, de los cuales 9.600 son de nacionalidad monegasca.

Más información Viaje por la Polonia judía

Bien es sabido que las apariencias engañan. Mónaco, independizado de Génova desde 1297, no forma parte de la Unión Europea pese a sus contactos más que frecuentes con Francia e Italia. Este factor, a priori, no supone ningún problema, o al menos antes no preocupaba a ningún visitante por el hábito de ir, a lo sumo, con un mapa para orientarse por sus calles. Pero los tiempos han cambiado y ahora mismo para muchos turistas resulta imprescindible disponer de internet para caminar con garantías. En mi caso confieso que suelo usar los mapas digitales como brújula base, para, a continuación, prescindir del móvil y así poder mirar bien aquello que piso sin condenarme a la pantalla.

El problema es que en Mónaco no puedes ir tan suelto —el roaming gratuito de la UE no se aplica de forma automática por ley—, al menos si es tu primera vez en el Principado, donde un exceso de confianza puede costarte una gran frustración, como fue mi caso tras bajar del tren, sentirme satisfecho por alcanzar el Casino de Montecarlo, que es el nombre de uno de los cuatro barrios del centro de Mónaco pese a confundirse por todo el conjunto, y luego soltarme hasta, literalmente, perderme en una serie de avenidas sin ninguna referencia visual válida para rehacer el camino y recuperar la cordura del itinerario.

Lo más grotesco de esa experiencia fue que pude entender con rotundidad mi fracaso al subir una cuesta e informarme un cartel de estar en Beausoleil, pueblo francés que junto a Montecarlo forma una sola aglomeración urbana. A partir de ese punto respiré hondo gracias a las vistas, perfectas para situarme y pasear sin necesidad de datos ni de conexión wifi al comprender la morfología de la ciudad.

Exterior del casino de Montecarlo. David Gee (Alamy / Cordon Press)

La clave de todo estriba, sobre todo para caminar sin riesgo a extraviarse, en salir de la estación por el sitio justo, que siempre es la Rue Grimaldi, e ir hasta la Avenue d’Ostende, desde la que cualquier ruta es fácil, si bien recomiendo ascenderla e ir hacia el Casino de Montecarlo porque siempre es el mejor punto de partida al ser un icono alejado del resto que sirve como Kilómetro cero hacia los demás.

Mónaco legalizó el juego en 1854 y necesitaba un edificio de postín para atraer a buscadores de fortuna que quisieran combinar la osadía con el prestigio de ganar dinero en un marco de veras incomparable, como lo fue el casino desde 1878, cuando Charles Garnier, autor de la Ópera de París, le confirió su actual aspecto. Este templo mundial de la apuesta, inmortalizado por Stefan Zweig en la novela 24 horas en la vida de una mujer (1924), ha proporcionado ingentes dividendos a la familia Grimaldi, si bien en nuestro siglo su facturación no es decisiva para las finanzas del Principado.

Desde el casino, con una plaza dispuesta para transitar entre el lujo y la egolatría contemporánea del selfi, lo mejor es volver a la Avenue d’Ostende, parándonos en cualquiera de sus pequeños miradores para aprehender mejor por dónde nos movemos sin marearnos por la enorme densidad de edificios entre imposibles rascacielos y hoteles de la Belle Époque afeados por estos excesos constructivos. Al final la vista se habitúa a los mismos porque cada sitio tiene su propia belleza, aunque aquí siempre es más hermoso mirar a la izquierda para admirar el Puerto de Hércules del barrio de La Condamine, que rodearemos para llegar al otro espectáculo que la vista nos ofrece en esta panorámica: Le Rocher, o la roca en las alturas donde se concentran los distintos poderes monegascos.

Vista de Le Rocher, donde se concentran los distintos poderes monegascos. Westend61 (getty images)

La encrucijada hacia esta meta se ubica, valga la redundancia, en el cruce de la Avenue d’Ostende con su paralela dedicada a John Fitzgerald Kennedy, que da paso al Quai dedicado a Alberto I, con comienzo y final capitalizado por dos estatuas que honran a leyendas del automovilismo. La primera es de William Grover, mientras la segunda, ya en las estribaciones de las escaleras hacia Le Rocher, es un homenaje al campeonísimo argentino de la especialidad Juan Manuel Fangio, quien cosechó dos victorias en el Gran Premio más famoso del circo de la F1.

Monumento en recuerdo del piloto argentino de Juan Manuel Fangio, en Mónaco. Paul Quayle (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Desde esta estatua, una de las más fotografiadas de nuestro recorrido, disponemos de un pequeño abanico de opciones para escalar hacia la roca, aunque mi consejo es ir por las avenidas du Port y de la Porte Neuve para no repetir nuestros pasos y no aburrirnos cuando regresemos de esta expedición, que tiene como cumbre el Palacio Principesco en su homónima plaza, donde cada día, a las 11.55 en punto, se produce el muy vitoreado cambio de guardia de los Carabineros del Príncipe.

El Palacio Principesco, ubicado en la plaza homónima.

La primera piedra de la residencia real se puso a finales del siglo XIII, remodelándose hasta finales de la decimonovena centuria, cuando aún se rodeaba de una rica vegetación en los alrededores, poco a poco rebajada sin desaparecer del todo pese al crecimiento de estos aledaños, que en nuestra época mezclan lo esencial de cualquier centro urbano con un apabullante número de tiendas dedicadas a vender baratijas y souvenirs. Lo mejor, como sospecharán, es parar poquito en esos negocios y, aquí sí, caracolear por las callecitas sin temor a descarriarse porque todo queda cerca, de los miradores a la catedral, construida en 1875 y firmada por el arquitecto Charles Lenormand, con una blanquísima fachada que oculta un rico interior dividido en tres naves, a rebosar de obras de arte, muchas de ellas provenientes del anterior templo, demolido como preludio a su completa renovación de estilo neorromántico.

La catedral de Nuestra Señora Inmaculada, conocida también como catedral de Mónaco. Barry Winiker (getty images)

De la catedral —lugar de entierro del príncipe Rainiero III y la princesa Grace— al último hito de este pequeñísimo país median menos de 300 metros. Se trata del Museo Oceanográfico, impulsado por el príncipe Alberto I, cuya fama de gran navegante se simboliza por este legado, abierto al público en marzo de 1910 y dirigido a partir de 1957 (y durante más de 30 años), en coincidencia con el auge turístico, por el comandante Jacques-Yves Cousteau, fundamental para armar el aparato pedagógico de la institución, muy en consonancia con el transmitido en sus documentales televisivos que tanta popularidad le dieron durante la segunda mitad del siglo pasado.

Mónaco no encierra muchas dificultades para el visitante y puede saborearse al detalle en pocas horas con la virtud añadida de conseguir que muchos se sientan menos dependientes de la tecnología por esa carambola de no poder usar los datos del móvil como en la Unión Europea. Ahora que terminamos les confesaré que claro, seguro encuentran alguna red wifi disponible brindada por las autoridades, pero créanme, si prescinden de teclear su contraseña ganarán tiempo y el privilegio de poder andar con el cuerpo bien erguido y los ojos fijos en el horizonte, algo que, por desgracia, cada vez es menos habitual en cualquier latitud del planeta.

World.title: Parents of euthanasia teen go to court over prosecution letter
World.content:
The parents of a 17-year-old girl who chose to die by euthanasia in 2023 due to incurable psychological suffering have gone to court to force public prosecutors to identify a group of doctors that wrote a damning letter about the case.

Their daughter Milou’s psychological struggles were documented in a 2023 documentary, which covered her wish to be granted the right to voluntary death and the aftermath that followed.

The case caused significant public controversy and a group of 14 doctors subsequently wrote a letter suggesting a criminal investigation should be launched against the parents and doctors involved in treating her.

They called on prosecutors to find out “to what extent those close to this vulnerable patient (…) influenced this young patient’s decision to choose euthanasia.” The writers of the letter did not know Milou or her personal background and had not spoken to her themselves.

Eight of the signatories of the letter are still unnamed. In a courtroom in The Hague on Tuesday, the mother of Milou recounted how that letter had led to daily threats and intimidation, requiring the police to guard their home.

“As a parent, losing your child and having to miss them forever is the worst thing that can happen to you,” the mother Mireille Verhoof told the court. “Being accused afterwards of inciting the death of your child or being complicit in her death is beyond description and unbearable.”

She also said her daughter had effectively been “abused” by anti-euthanasia campaigners, who dismissed their integrity to further a political agenda.

The family’s lawyer Richard Korver also said that the people behind the letter should not be able to use their professional authority to make serious accusations and at the same time claim anonymity, reported to Omroep Brabant.

The public prosecution department still does not want to release the names so as to avoid further conflict and ensure people can bring judicial complaints in confidence. It also disputes that the letter was meant as a formal request for criminal proceedings.

The federation of doctors KNMG also condemned the letter, describing it as “indecent and unacceptable.” The court’s decision on the release of the names is expected on September 3.

If you or someone close to you is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. In the Netherlands, call 113 or 0800-0113 (free) for 24/7 support, or visit 113.nl, where the chat service is available in English.

World.title: Dutch shops to stock more GM food after EU relaxes rules in 2028
World.content:
More genetically modified food is likely to appear in Dutch stores when rules on licensing and labelling are relaxed in two years’ time.

The European parliament passed a law before the summer recess allowing food retailers to stock products containing GM ingredients without labelling them as such, as long as they account for less than 1% of the contents.

The more flexible law was brought in to offset the effect of stricter limits on pesticides, which the EU wanted to halve by 2030, so that growers could use genetic modification to make their crops more resistant to parasites.

But two years ago the EU dropped the pesticides bill, which commission president Ursula von der Leyen said had become “a symbol of polarisation”, while still going ahead with the relaxation of GM rules.

Food products that have been significantly changed by genetic modification will still have to be licensed and labelled under the current rules.

Michelle Habets, a researcher at the Rathenau Institute, a science and technology think tank based in The Hague, said the more flexible rules risked undermining public confidence in supermarkets and other food retailers.

She told NOS she had spoken to dozens of consumers about the new law while it was passing through the European parliament. “Everyone agreed that genetically modified crops should be labelled,” she said.

“People admitted they don’t always study every label in the supermarket, but they think transparency is important, as is the freedom of choice for people who don’t want to eat those crops for whatever reason.”

Jeroen Candel, associate professor of food and agricultural policy at Wageningen University, said GM crops could bring benefits by reducing the need for pesticides, but added a note of caution.

“The new law is based on the idead that we can optimalise the current system of agriculture with new technology,” he said. “But if we do that, we are maintaining a system that is not sustainable in terms of climate and biodiversity.”

World.title: Dutch media attack “chilling” fines for slimming drugs coverage
World.content:
Dutch media companies have been hit with fines running into the tens of millions of euros after inspectors ruled that their reporting on weight loss drugs such as Ozempic amounted to advertising.

Editors described the penalties, issued by the health department’s inspectorate IGJ, as “bizarre” and an attack on press freedom.

The verdicts covered newspapers across the range and political spectrum of Dutch media including NRC, the Volkskrant, the Telegraaf and AD.

The inspectors said the coverage of medicines such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro was too positive because it reported that the benefits of the drugs went beyond treating diabetes, the only condition they are prescribed for in the Netherlands.

The Dutch Medicines Act bans advertising for prescription medicines. The IGJ said it had issued around 20 fines between 2023 for breaching the law, not just to media companies.

Science reporting

The inspectorate would not go into individual cases, but DPG Media, one of the two main news publishers in the Netherlands, said it had been fined €48,500 in April for two articles in local newspaper De Stentor and lifestyle magazine Flair, and another €51,000 this month for articles in the Volkskrant and AD.

Mediahuis was fined a total of €132,000 this month for articles in NRC’s science section and the Telegraaf.

The IGJ said: “We weigh up the facts carefully in each case, including the interests of patients. In the case of media coverage we look at the whole picture: content, context, images and audio. It’s not a tick list.”

The journalists’ union NVJ said it was “shocked” that the inspectorate had imposed fines on reporters “who regularly write about medicines and have no other interest than informing the public.”

General secretary Thomas Bruning called for talks with the health ministry to discuss the sanctions. “This makes it impossible for journalists to report on this subject in a normal fashion,” he said. “We are taking it very seriously.”

Press freedom

Pieter Klok, editor of the Volkskrant, said he respected the ban on advertising and the IGJ’s right to enforce it. “But I don’t think it should be applied to journalism, unless you can show it’s been paid for,” he said.

Telegraaf editor Kamran Ullah said it would have a “huge chilling effect” on journalists reporting on health issues.

“That goes not just for large news organisations like us, but maybe even more for smaller titles and freelancers. Big publishers can pay these fines, but a fine of more than €100,000 is the equivalent of two journalists’ annual salary.

“That’s a real infringement of press freedom, because if we have to pay these fines, we can’t employ as many journalists.”

World.title: AI share prices lift household investments to a record high
World.content:
Dutch households’ investments in the stock market are worth more than ever amid the boom in enthusiasm around AI and technology, the central bank DNB has said.

The total value of shares, funds and bonds held by Dutch households rose about 12% in the second quarter to a record €234.2 billion. It is the sharpest rise in a single quarter since the bank started tracking the figures in 2018.

The gain was almost entirely down to rising share prices, which lifted the value of investments people already owned. Households did not buy more shares – over the quarter they actually sold more than they bought.

ASML, Shell and SpaceX

The fervour around AI adoption has helped ASML, the chip-machine maker, become the most valuable holding in Dutch portfolios, at about €6.1 billion. It pushed Shell, long the most popular investment, into second place at around €4.1 billion, with Rabobank third.

The quarter also saw a massive stock-market debut with Elon Musk’s space company SpaceX listed in New York in June, with Dutch households buying €169 million of its shares in the first month – the most they have ever put into a newly listed company since DNB’s records began.

Many did not hold on for long. A large part was sold again within weeks, probably to lock in the early gains, leaving €71 million still invested by the end of June.

Despite all the gains, investing remains a minority practice in the Netherlands. Only about a quarter of the country’s 8.4 million households invest at all, and the Dutch still keep far more in the bank – around €600 billion in savings – than in the markets.

World.title: Berendsen: Netherlands “disapproves” of new Trump ICC sanctions
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch foreign minister Tom Berendsen has criticised the latest sanctions imposed by the Trump administration against officials of the International Criminal Court, based in The Hague.

Berendsen said international courts “must be able to freely carry out their mandates” after the measures were taken against the court’s president, Tomoko Akane, and senior prosecutor Abdoulaye Saye.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Akane and Saye had been “directly engaged in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government ⁠has not consented to ICC jurisdiction.”

Seye was a member of the prosecution team that drafted the arrest warrants against Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s former defence minister Yoav Gallant 18 months ago.

Shortly afterwards Donald Trump issued an executive order authorising sanctions against ICC officials, such as freezing their bank accounts in the US and shutting them out of international payment systems.

The US and Israel are not signatories to the ICC’s founding statutes, but the government of Palestine is. The ICC ruled in 2021 that Gaza and the West Bank fell under its jurisdiction.

Continued support

Berendsen said in a post on social media site X, formerly Twitter: “The Netherlands disapproves of the latest sanctions against officials and staff of the International Criminal Court.”

He went on to offer to meet Akane “to discuss our continued support.” Berendsen did not directly condemn the US government’s actions.

The Netherlands disapproves of the latest sanctions against officials and staff of the International Criminal Court. International courts and tribunals must be able to freely carry out their mandates. 1/2 — Tom Berendsen (@ministerBZ) August 18, 2026



Akane said last year that the sanctions would “rapidly undermine the court’s operations”, while in recent months Rubio has stepped up his rhetoric against the ICC, accusing it of “waging a war against our country” and vowing to dismantle it “brick by brick”.

World.title: Higher oil prices drive up Dutch industrial turnover
World.content:
Dutch industrial turnover rose 8.4% in the second quarter, the biggest year-on-year rise since the end of 2022. But it was driven mainly by higher oil prices rather than a real recovery, figures from national statistics agency CBS show.

Prices across industry were 5% higher than a year ago, so more than half of the rise reflects costlier goods rather than higher sales. Last year, turnover had fallen 0.7%.

The growth was also uneven, with refineries and the chemical industry taking in 31.2% more than a year earlier, and the oil industry alone up 83% as its selling prices rose 40.5%.

The higher oil prices stem from disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been largely shut since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. With few ships getting through, prices have risen – the same reason petrol has been so expensive in the Netherlands this year.

Not every sector grew. Food, drink and tobacco fell furthest, with turnover down 6.7%, mainly because selling prices dropped. Shoppers are unlikely to see that in the supermarket yet, as there are many steps between factory and shelf.

Manufacturers are more optimistic about the months ahead, with more expecting higher turnover than at any point since mid-2022. Even so, many still cannot find enough workers, and slightly more industrial companies went bankrupt than a year earlier, CBS said.

World.title: “Exceptional” 17th-century sketchbook donated to Rijksmuseum
World.content:
A 17th-century sketchbook containing 30 drawings has been hailed as a rare find after it was donated to the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

Several of the sketches have been attributed to the Frisian painter Rombould Uylenburgh, who was a well-known artist in his day but fell into obscurity following his death in 1627 or 1628.

The book is known as the Van Eeghen sketchbook, after the family of Amsterdam merchants who owned it for three centuries. The sketches, some of which were made on blue paper, have retained their colour because the book has not been on display.

The Rijksmuseum said it was unusual for an artist’s sketchbook from the 17th century to survive intact for so long. More commonly, the drawings are torn out and sold individually, or lost.

Only two sketches and a handful of paintings by Uylenburgh were thought to have survived when the sketchbook resurfaced in 1935.

The drawings in the book were only attributed to him in 2013, after the owner saw they were similar to one of the artist’s works in the Rijksmuseum’s collection.

Uylenburgh was born in Friesland in 1580 but spent most of his life in Poland after his family emigrated to Krakow. He because the court painter of King Sigismund III Vasa and went on to build a successful career in the port city of Danzig.

His brother, Hendrik, returned to the Dutch Republic and based himself in Amsterdam. By 1625 had established himself as Rembrandt’s main art dealer and is believed to have introduced the painter to his cousin, Saskia van Uylenburgh, who married Rembrandt in 1633.

The Van Eeghen sketchbook is the focus of a display in the museum from August 19 until November 29.

World.title: Holidaymakers warned not to bring home “destructive” beetle
World.content:
The Dutch food standards watchdog NVWA has urged returning holidaymakers not to bring back foreign invaders after a Japanese beetle was found in a freight shipment from Italy.

The insect was found dead in a plastic container that was being transported from a region of Italy where Japanese beetles are known to live.

The NVWA set traps in the container to see if any live beetles had crept inside, but none were found. But the agency told people coming back from southern Europe and transport companies to be alert and report any specimens they found.

“The NVWA is explicitly asking trading and logistics companies to be alert for beetles hitching a lift when they travel to or through the named areas,” the agency said in a statement.

“Do not in any event leave the doors and windows of your vehicle open for longer than necessary and try to check goods and packing for beetles before departure if possible.“

Japanese beetles are not considered a pest in their native country, where their numbers are controlled by natural predators.

But in recent years they have been spotted in Italy, Croatia, Switzerland, Germany and the Azores. The German province of Hessen is the closest area to the Netherlands with an established population.

They are regarded as highly destructive because they feed on a wide range of vegetation. Adult beetles will devour leaves and stems of plants, while their larvae eat grass roots and weeds.

The NVWA has also published advice on its website advising people how to tell Japanese beetles apart from similar looking native species.

World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she came to parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is the main opponent of PiS. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.title: FedEx-led €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost wins EU approval
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. The proportion of children taking Catholic catechism in schools has continued to fall but remains a majority https://t.co/5bu35hzJ7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
